thread:
pagerduty-bot: URGENT: Multiple 5xx/timeouts detected on /v1/generate (us-east-1). Error rate spike: 12% over last 3m. Paging alice_oncall. Incident severity: P1. Links: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/1987654321 :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: On it. joining now. Can someone grab tracing and gateway logs? @ben_sre do you see anything in scheduler metrics?

ben_sre: grabbing metrics. batch_queue_len for inference-scheduler (us-east) spiked to 1.2k, avg queue wait ~620ms, p95 latency for scheduler enqueue up to 980ms. A bunch of long-context requests are blocking small ones (head-of-line). Looks like batch formation is waiting for large requests -> HOL.

carla_runtime: confirming - the new batching heuristics rollout from last night changed wait_ms from 12 -> 40 for higher throughput. That increases join time for small requests when large ones come in. Might be the tuning interacting poorly with current traffic skew.

dan_ingress: Gateway logs show increasing upstream 502/504s and timeouts to runtime nodes, correlated with queue depth. Example excerpt: ```
[2026-03-15T15:12:03Z] gateway us-east node-7: upstream_timeout route=/v1/generate status=504 backend=runtime-12 queue_len=1135
[2026-03-15T15:12:07Z] gateway us-east node-5: upstream_error route=/v1/generate status=502 backend=runtime-4 queue_len=1198
```

eve_support: Any customer-facing impact known? CS slack shows two customers opened chats: acme-corp and beta-saas. Both report intermittent latency and failures. Frank, can you coordinate notices?

frank_custops: drafting message. ETA 10m. We'll say: "We are investigating elevated errors affecting generation endpoints in us-east. Some requests may see timeouts. Engineers are actively mitigating. No data loss observed."

alice_oncall: Triage plan: 1) Immediate mitigation to reduce head-of-line by disabling the longer wait_ms and forcing smaller max_batch_size for /v1/generate. 2) If errors persist, reroute traffic for /v1/generate to dedicated pool (dedicated-rt-01) and enable fallback model variant (quantized-small) for non-critical customers. 3) Postmortem and config rollback after stable. Assigning ben_sre primary.

ben_sre: Doing step 1 now. Will flip batching policy for route /v1/generate: set wait_ms=8, max_batch_size=32. Command: ```
curl -X POST "https://config.redwood/api/v1/route-config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","wait_ms":8,"max_batch_size":32}'
``` Applying...

deploy-bot: config-change: route /v1/generate updated by ben_sre. change_id=chg-9872.

ben_sre: Rolling out change to us-east. Observability: queue_len dropping from 1200 -> 400 within 90s. p95 enqueue down to ~210ms. Still seeing some 504s from in-flight requests.

carla_runtime: Recommend also temporarily disabling prefix KV caching for very long-context requests — KV cache is keeping large state and causing scheduling fragmentation. Toggle: ```
redwoodctl runtime set-feature --feature prefix-kv-cache --route "/v1/generate" --enabled=false
``` Doing that for 2 clusters now.

dan_ingress: While those changes propagate, starting reroute plan in parallel. Will open canary to dedicated-rt-01 for 10% of traffic for the next 5m, escalate if stable. Command: ```
opsctl traffic shift --route "/v1/generate" --to dedicated-rt-01 --percent 10
```

deploy-bot: traffic-shift: /v1/generate -> dedicated-rt-01 10% by dan_ingress. shift_id=ts-3344

ben_sre: After disabling long wait and kv cache, queue_len down to ~120, error rate fell to 2.1%. Canary to dedicated pool holding steady with 0.3% errors. Looks like primary issue was batching heuristics + large-context requests.

eve_support: Notifying customers now with updated ETA. frank_custops, please include that we've applied a mitigation and we're monitoring.

frank_custops: Sent message to acme-corp & beta-saas. Logged impacted customers list and opened support-level incident tickets.

alice_oncall: Good. Keep monitoring for 30m. If error rate stays <1% and queue length stable <50, we'll mark mitigated. ben_sre continue as owner, carla_runtime do a config postmortem and revert the heuristic rollout for next canary. dan_ingress work with infra to create a safer default for wait_ms.

ben_sre: Affirmative. Creating follow-up runbook entries: - add HOL detection alert on per-route p99 enqueue time - emergency flag to force immediate small-batch policy.

carla_runtime: Will rollback the 40ms default in the rollout and force a staged canary. Also will add unit test to simulate skew with heavy long-ctx requests.

dan_ingress: I'll add gateway-level quick-fallback: if upstream queue_len > 800 then route to fallback pool automatically (feature flag). Implementing toggle now: ```
opsctl feature-flag set --name gateway-fallback-high-queue --value true
```

deploy-bot: feature-flag change recorded by dan_ingress. flag_id=ff-221

ben_sre: Monitoring: at 15:40 UTC queue_len steady ~28, error rate 0.9% over 5m, downstream 504s ~1/min (normal). Closing active mitigation. Will keep thread open for handoff.

alice_oncall: Oncall handoff: I'm stepping off in ~20m. ben_sre you'll take primary for the next 3h monitoring window. If anything regresses escalate to oncall manager.

ben_sre: Taking handoff. Documenting timeline and actions in incident tracker. Preliminary impact: peak error rate 12%, approximately 2.8k failed requests/min at peak, impacted 2 major customers (acme-corp, beta-saas) with transient latency/errors. No customer data lost.

frank_custops: Customers informed. Will follow up with a more detailed timeline and once root cause confirmed.

alice_oncall: Good job team. Assigning postmortem owners: carla_runtime (root cause & rollout safeguards), ben_sre (live mitigation and alerting gaps), dan_ingress (gateway fallback feature & auto-reroute tests). We'll sync tomorrow 10:00am PT. Marking incident as mitigated in the alerting system but keeping incident channel open for notes. :white_check_mark:
